CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.uploadPhotos iterates the request-controlled List<MultipartFile> at line 69 without checking its element count. Each iteration performs image-header processing and database operations through uploadPhoto (70) and a subsequent read (73). The configured max-files-per-upload at application.properties:30 is never consumed by production Java. The 50 MB multipart request cap bounds bytes, not the number of small parts and database operations; exploiting this route requires upload authentication. No infinite loop is claimed.

CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Explanation: The public gallery GET invokes getAllPhotos, which materializes an unbounded List<Photo> from a native SELECT including every photo_data BLOB (PhotoRepository:23-29); Photo.photoData is an eagerly loaded byte[] without lazy Basic loading. Aggregate allocation is proportional to all uploaded content, with no pagination or aggregate byte limit. Per-file upload limits do not bound the full dataset. Once authenticated uploads populate a sufficiently large gallery, an anonymous gallery request can cause heap exhaustion; repeated large-read requests increase pressure. This is database-driven aggregate allocation, not an unchecked new byte[requestSize] primitive.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: SecurityConfig configures HTTP Basic authentication but installs no authentication success/failure audit handler or event listener. Authentication rejection occurs in Spring Security before HomeController/DetailController log calls; no application authentication-event listener or access-log configuration exists. In the Docker profile Spring web logs are WARN and Spring Security has no explicit audit logging configuration. Thus unsuccessful login attempts lack an application-configured security audit record identifying the attempted user and outcome. This is absence of configured authentication auditing, not a claim that all application actions are unlogged; upload/delete outcomes are logged.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto trusts the client-supplied Content-Type allowlist (line 87). If ImageIO finds no reader (lines 125-142), the method nevertheless saves the unvalidated bytes (lines 154-166); non-IO parsing exceptions also continue (149-152). Thus arbitrary non-image content labeled image/jpeg can be stored and publicly retrieved by PhotoFileController.servePhoto (75-83), without confirming an accepted image format. This confirms absent server-side file-content validation, not execution of uploaded code; response is restricted to configured image MIME types.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: upload.js handleFiles incorporates attacker-influenced File.name into validation error strings (73,75), which showErrors inserts as HTML without escaping at 216-218. A crafted filename containing an HTML element/event handler is parsed in the gallery origin when a victim selects or drops it; this error path runs before any authenticated upload is required. This is a filename-triggered DOM XSS requiring victim file interaction, not evidence of automatic cross-user stored XSS on page reload. Server-returned filenames also reach unescaped createPhotoCard HTML at 185-189 and insertAdjacentHTML at 157.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component. Without sufficient removal or quoting of SQL syntax in user-controllable inputs, the generated SQL query can cause those inputs to be interpreted as SQL instead of ordinary user data.
CweFindings.Explanation: The startup SQLPlus here-documents substitute environment-controlled APP_USER_UPPER into SQL string literals (01-create-user.sh:25) and a dynamic EXECUTE IMMEDIATE CREATE USER statement at line 28; the environment-supplied schema password is interpolated into the same dynamic SQL without SQL/PLSQL quote escaping. A quote-bearing configured value can alter the generated PL/SQL statement under the privileged bootstrap connection. Preconditions: control of deployment environment variables; no HTTP input reaches this bootstrap path. Application PhotoRepository queries themselves use fixed statements and bound parameters. Credential values intentionally omitted.
